Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //wtvw.dilg.com.ph 07 JAN DILG OPINION NO. MAYOR JAIME E. ESMERALDA Igbaras, Iloilo Dear Mayor Esmeralda This has reference to your 02 September 2019 letter requesting clarification on your authority to practice your medical profession. In reply to thereto, we would like to invite your attention to the express provisions of Section 90 of the Local Government Code, which provides: "SECTION 90. Practice of Profession.- profession or engaginq in any occupation other than the exercise Of Cunctions as local chief executives (b) Sangguniang members may practice their professions, engage in any occupation, or teach in schools except during session hours: Provided, That sangguniang members who are also members of the Bar shall not: (1) (2) (3) (4) Appear as counsel before any court in any civil case wherein a local government unit or any office, agency, or instrumentality of the government is the adverse party; Appear as counsel in any criminal case wherein an officer or employee of the national or local government is accused of an offense committed in relation to his office; Collect any fee for their appearance in administrative proceedings involving the local government unit of which he is an official; and Use property and personnel of the government except when the sanggunian member concerned is defending the interest of the government. Doctors of medicine mav practice their profession even during Official hours Of work only on occasions f mer enc • Pr vided ha h ffiils nc rn do not derive monetary compensation tfrerefrom. " (Emphasis ours)

From the aforeqouted provisions of law, governors, mayors of cities and municipalities are prohibited from practicing their professions or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. The rationale is that their offices (governor/mayor) is a full time job. To acquiesce them to practice their profession e.g. a lawyer, doctor or engineer, may result to conflict of interest. They may be allured to allot more time to the practice of profession than to the discharge of the duties and functions of his office. Constantly, this Department opined that the prohibition is absolute. Clearly, under paragraph (c) of the cited provisions, being a doctor, you are allowed to practice your profession even during official hours of work, but only on occasions of emergency, and provided further, you do not obtain monetary compensation therefrom. In relation thereto, Section 7 of Republic Act No. 6713, provides: "Section 7. Prohibited acts and transactions. — In addition to acts and omissions of public officials and employees now prescribed in the Constitution and existing laws, the following shall constitute prohibited acts and transactions of any public official and employee and are hereby declared to be unlawful: xxx xxx xxx (b) Outside employment and other activities related thereto-Public officials and employees during their incumbency shall not: xxx xxx xxx (2) Engage in the private practice Of their profession le au horized th on tit tio or law rovided th such practice will not conflict or tend to conflict with their supplied) Foregoing considered, indubitably, you are prohibited from practicing your profession as doctor except, as emphasized, on occasions of emergency. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, BY THE AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY MARIV L C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Und ecretary for Local Governmen CC: RD Ariel O.
